newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's future leader leaves for Beijing talks.
newsitem.headline: HK's future leader leaves for Beijing talks.

text.p: The future leader of Hong Kong left the territory on Saturday for Beijing where he is due to hold his first set of working level talks with Chinese officials.

Tung Chee-hwa, who declined to comment before flying to the Chinese capital, said earlier that his one-day visit would focus on government funding and the legal status of the controversial post-colonial legislature which China will install when it takes over Hong Kong from Britain on July 1.

The 59-year-old former shipping magnate said he would discuss the constitutional status of the provisional legislature, which faces a legal challenge from Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy group, the Democratic Party.
Tung did not say, however, whether he would ask the Chinese parliament to pass a law to endorse the interim assembly in order to shield it against a legal challenge.
The Democratic Party argues that it is illegal for two rival legislatures to sit simultaneously.
The provisional legislature, chosen under Beijing's supervision on December 21, is to reverse democratic reforms in the territory introduced by colonial governor Chris Patten.
The Democratic Party fared the best in 1995 Legislative Council elections but its deputies will lose their seats when Beijing dissolves the chamber.

The trip is Tung's second to Beijing since his appointment as chief executive-designate on December 11. He was received by President Jiang Zemin, Premier Li Peng and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen during his first visit after his selection.
Tung is expected to return to Hong Kong on Sunday morning.
